title: New Zealand Hit by Double Injury Blow Ahead of India T20I Series
excerpt: Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes are ruled out of the five-match series; Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner join the Black Caps squad for the opener in Christchurch on October 22.
body:
• New Zealand have lost batter Mark Chapman and fast bowler Zak Foulkes to injury for the five-match T20I series against India, New Zealand Cricket confirmed on Friday.
  • Chapman tore his left hamstring playing in the European T20 Premier League last month and is expected to recover in time for the ODI series; Foulkes injured his right hip flexor at a Canterbury training session, with no return timeline set.
  • All-rounder Josh Clarkson and fast bowler Blair Tickner have been called up as replacements, with Tickner set to play his first T20 international in more than three years.
  • The five-match T20I series begins in Christchurch on October 22, kicking off an all-format tour that also includes five ODIs and two Tests — a rematch of the 2026 T20 World Cup final, which India won by 96 runs.

New Zealand's preparations for their white-ball showdown with India have been dealt a double injury blow, with batter Mark Chapman and fast bowler Zak Foulkes ruled out of the five-match T20I series. New Zealand Cricket confirmed the news on Friday, naming all-rounder Josh Clarkson and fast bowler Blair Tickner as replacements.

The injuries

Chapman suffered a left hamstring tear while playing in the European T20 Premier League last month, representing the Belfast Wolves in the league's inaugural edition, and will be sidelined for the entire T20I series. There is better news on his prognosis: he is on track to be available for the one-day internationals against India, which follow the T20s.

Foulkes's situation is less clear. The fast bowler injured his right hip flexor during a recent Canterbury men's training session, and his return-to-play timeline is yet to be determined, according to NZC.

The replacements

Into the 16-member squad come Clarkson and Tickner — two very different stories. Clarkson was part of the second-string New Zealand side that played Bangladesh during the IPL 2026 window and offers seam-bowling depth in the middle order. Tickner, meanwhile, is set for a long-awaited return: the pacer has not played a T20 international in more than three years. Last year a shoulder injury sidelined him from action; his previous T20I appearance, against Pakistan, saw him finish as the pick of the bowlers with three wickets for 33 runs.

"I'm gutted for Mark and Zak and I wish them both a smooth recovery. We're fortunate to be able to lean on the expertise of Josh and Blair."

— Rob Walter, New Zealand head coach

"I know they're both very excited to be involved in what's shaping up to be an epic T20 series," Walter added, looking ahead to a contest that needs little extra fuel.

A series with a storyline

The T20I series opens in Christchurch on October 22 and is the opening act of an all-format tour: five T20s, five ODIs in November, and two Tests. The stakes carry recent history — India and New Zealand met in the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup earlier this year, when India registered a comprehensive 96-run triumph.

For India, the series is another chance to measure their T20 depth against the side they beat in the final. For New Zealand, already without Chapman and Foulkes, it is an early test of squad resilience — and an audition for Clarkson and Tickner to cement places beyond the tour.

The New Zealand T20I squad

Mitchell Santner (captain), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Josh Clarkson, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Matt Henry, Bevon Jacobs, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner.

What to watch

The first T20 in Christchurch will reveal how New Zealand reshape their XI without Chapman's middle-order hitting and Foulkes's new-ball swing. If Tickner rediscovers his Pakistan form and Clarkson makes the all-rounder's case, the "double blow" could turn into a depth-building exercise ahead of the ODIs and Tests — where Chapman, at least, is expected to return.
